title: PROTECTED_FILES matches by basename with no notion of tree: 144 of 234 newly-blocked commands are agents writing legitimate /tmp test fixtures
body:
`PROTECTED_FILES` in the Bash write guard matches by **basename**, with no notion of which tree a path is in. Measured on a 5,060-command real corpus during #1120: of 234 commands the hardened guard newly blocks, **144 are interpreter writes to `workflow-state.json` under `mkdtemp` or `/tmp`.**

Every one of those 144 is a **true positive against the rule as written** and a **false positive against intent**. They are test fixtures. An agent building a fixture for the very guard that refuses it is doing exactly the right thing and getting stopped.

## Why this is now a design gap rather than a deferral

`specs/HOOK-ARCHITECTURE-SPEC.md` already defers the same question for the `*.hook.ts` arm. It now bites a second arm. **A deferral that recurs in a second place is a design gap**, and the enumerate-by-basename approach is what both arms inherit.

The 144 is also an understatement of the friction: it counts one corpus on one machine. Every consumer writing a fixture named `workflow-state.json` anywhere on disk inherits the same refusal, and they will not have the corpus to discover why.

## Why it was not fixed inside #1120

Scoping to the project root makes every guard decision depend on correctly resolving that root. That dependency was **broken until today**: #1129 was exactly this failure — `nonCanonicalRoots()` compared a canonicalised path against an un-`resolve()`d root, and a root spelled with a trailing slash or a `.` segment broke containment in ship.js's `collectDestination`, measured at **5 of 6 spellings**. The production fix merged as `1e4f1b57`; the test lock-in is **#1165**.

Building root-relative protection on top of root resolution that stabilised the same day is the wrong order. That is the only reason this is a separate issue and not part of #1145.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A protected artifact is identified by its path **relative to the project root**, not by basename
- [ ] A write to a same-named file outside the project root is allowed, and there is a witness case for it
- [ ] A write to the real artifact is still refused, including when the root is spelled non-canonically — reuse `resolve()`-then-compare from #1129 rather than writing a second copy
- [ ] An **unresolvable** root refuses rather than allows. This is the fail-open risk the change introduces and it must be a named case, not an implicit default
- [ ] Re-run the 5,060-command corpus: the 144 go to allowed, and the count of newly-blocked **real** writes does not drop

## Predict before measuring

State an integer for how many of the 234 clear, and a case list, before re-running the corpus. The expected answer is 144, which makes this a good calibration: a result that is not 144 means either the scoping is wrong or the original count was.

## Dependency

**#1165** — the #1129 lock-in tests — should land first, so the canonicalisation this relies on cannot silently regress underneath it.

Found during #1120. Reported by the implementing agent as explicitly out of scope and handed up rather than taken quietly, which was the right call.

title: `PROTECTED_FILES` matches by basename, so BashWriteGuard refuses 144 legitimate test fixtures under `/tmp` and `mkdtemp`
body:
## The measurement

Sweeping 5,060 unique real commands (extracted from 35,040 transcripts on this machine) through `lib/bash-write-guard.ts` as merged in #1145:

| Reading | Count |
|---|---|
| newly blocked vs the pre-#1145 guard | 234 |
| of those, interpreter writes to a gate-artifact basename under `/tmp` or `mkdtemp` | **144** |

Those 144 are **true positives against the rule as written** and false positives against intent. They are agents writing `workflow-state.json` fixtures into a scratch directory — exactly the right thing to do — and being refused because the guard matches a basename with no notion of which tree it is in.

`PROTECTED_FILES` is `['workflow-state.json', '.gate-salt', '/witnesses/']`, tested with `String.includes` against a resolved-ish target string. A fixture at `/var/folders/.../T/rg-abc123/workflow-state.json` matches as readily as the real one at the project root.

## Why this is not a quick fix, and why it should not ride along with a guard patch

1. **Blast radius is the whole guard, not one arm.** Basename matching is what lets the guard work with zero configuration in any consumer repo. Replacing it with root-relative matching makes *every* decision depend on correctly resolving the project root, in a PreToolUse hook that must also decide correctly when the root cannot be resolved at all.

2. **That dependency stabilised only on 2026-10-22.** #1129 was precisely this failure: `nonCanonicalRoots()` compared a canonicalised path against an un-`resolve()`d root, so a root spelled with a trailing slash or a `.` segment broke containment in `collectDestination` — measured, 5 of 6 spellings. The fix landed as `1e4f1b57`; **the test lock-in is #1165 and is still open.** Building root-scoped protection on top of root resolution that has no regression test yet is the wrong order.

3. **The 144 deserve their own number.** A false-positive class with a measured denominator (234 newly blocked, 5,060 swept) is the strongest kind of issue to prioritise, and folding it into a bypass fix would bury it.

## This is no longer a deferral — it is a design gap

`specs/HOOK-ARCHITECTURE-SPEC.md` already defers exactly this question for the `*.hook.ts` arm: *"The `*.hook.ts` arm is still unscoped … settle that before `deployToConsumers`."* It now bites a second arm, in a different mechanism, with a measured cost.

A deferral that recurs in an arm nobody wrote it for is not a deferral any more; it is an unstated design decision — "protected names are global" — that was never chosen, only inherited. The spec note should be promoted from a per-arm caveat to a module-level decision, resolved either way and written down.

## Options, not a recommendation

- **Scope to the project root.** Clears all 144. Requires the guard to resolve a root, and to decide what to do when it cannot — refusing on UNMEASURED is defensible for a guard but changes behaviour in every unscaffolded tree.
- **Exempt well-known scratch prefixes** (`/tmp`, `/var/folders`, `mkdtemp` results, `TMPDIR`). Cheaper and needs no root, but it is an allowlist — and #1120's whole finding was that the previous allowlist had six of eleven entries with no recorded justification.
- **Do nothing and document it.** The 144 are refusals of real work; agents route around a guard that does this, which is the failure mode `WRITE_INTENT`'s docblock already warns about.

## Depends on

- #1165 — regression lock-in for the root-resolution fix `1e4f1b57`. Should land first if the scoping option is chosen.

## Context

- #1120 / PR #1145 — the rework that produced the measurement.
- `.claude/rules/checks-must-be-able-to-fail.md` — "a guard tuned so wide that people work around it protects nothing".
